newsitem.title: UK: GEC says pretax profit for first 4 mos ahead.
newsitem.headline: GEC says pretax profit for first 4 mos ahead.

text.p: General Electric Co Plc (GEC) reported on Friday that pretax profits for the first four months of the financial year were up on the same period in 1995 and also announced a rise in the order book.
The news was given at the annual meeting, the event at which long-standing GEC managing director Lord Weinstock will step down from the post after 33 years in the job.
GEC added "key units continue to win new business at a satisfactory rate."

GEC chairman Lord Prior told shareholders "...higher operating profits were earned from similar sales, although interest income declined as a result of reduced cash holdings and lower interest rates."
It said the company continued to invest in technological advances and ventures. It said the cash content of new investments in some of its ventures this year amounted to 300 million stg.
On the discussions between GEC and Alcatel Alsthom regarding the possible merger of GEC Alsthom and Framatome, Prior said the move would "enhance the industrial potential" of both firms.
The chairman said the industrial group's talks were proceeding on disposal of small units and pursuit of small acquisitions and ventures.
The GEC AGM will be Weinstock's last as managing director, though he will stay on in an advisory capacity.
His successor is George Simpson, who joins on Monday from LucasVarity Plc.
Simpson's last act as chief executive of the former Lucas Industries was to negotiate a merger with Varity Corp of the U.S.
